You're sourcing real key art for 5 games on Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting marketing site, staging tree at /opt/nxeon-staging — work ONLY in staging). This directly follows a bug found and fixed earlier today: a page was using a hardcoded Rust game photo on an unrelated page — the lesson is REAL, CORRECT, per-game art only, never placeholder or mismatched images.

The 5 games: Dragonwilds (RuneScape: Dragonwilds), Sunkenland, Abiotic Factor (slug `abioticfactor`), Core Keeper, Icarus. Check `lib/games.ts` at /opt/nxeon-staging for their exact `GAME_ART_SLUG` keys (the filename convention other games use).

Existing convention: check `public/games/art/` — existing games have `{slug}_hero.jpg` (wide hero/background image), `{slug}_poster.jpg` (portrait/box-art style), and often `{slug}_logo.png` (transparent logo). Look at a couple of existing examples to confirm exact dimensions/aspect ratios/format expected (check how they're rendered — e.g. `ModsTemplate.tsx` or a single-game landing component — for `object-cover`/`aspect-` classes that imply expected proportions).

For each of the 5 games, source REAL official promotional art — the standard, legitimate approach used across the game-hosting industry is Steam's public CDN, which serves official capsule/header/library images for every Steam store page (e.g. `https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/{appid}/header.jpg`, `library_hero.jpg`, `capsule_616x353.jpg`, etc. — these are Steam's own publicly-served marketing assets, standard practice for hosting sites to display since they're advertising a game the customer is choosing to play). Find each game's correct Steam App ID (WebSearch/SteamDB), then fetch appropriately high-resolution official art:
- A wide/landscape image for the `_hero.jpg` slot (library hero or a wide screenshot from the store page)
- A portrait/box-art image for the `_poster.jpg` slot (the library capsule or vertical capsule art)
- A transparent/clean logo if the game has one readily available (skip if not cleanly available — don't fabricate one)

Download and save these into `public/games/art/` using the EXACT naming convention already used (e.g. `dragonwilds_hero.jpg`, `dragonwilds_poster.jpg`). Verify each downloaded image actually shows the correct game (open/check dimensions and that the fetch succeeded with real image bytes, not a 404 page or placeholder) before considering that game done — do NOT save a broken/wrong image just to check a box. Match existing file sizes/dimensions reasonably (resize/compress if a source image is huge, to match the site's existing image weight conventions — check a couple of existing files' sizes as a rough target).

If any game's art genuinely isn't findable at good quality (rare for a real Steam-listed game, but possible for something obscure), report that specific gap clearly rather than using a low-quality or wrong substitute.

Report back per-game: art sourced (yes/no per hero/poster/logo), source URL used, final file size/dimensions, and any gaps. Under 300 words, a clear table.

Gap: Dragonwilds is Early Access and Steam hasn't generated a vertical library capsule for it (confirmed via the store page and appdetails API — only `header`/`capsule_616x353`/`library_hero` exist, no `library_600x900`, and no `logo.png`). For the poster I used an official 1920x1080 in-game screenshot from the same Steam app page (appid 1374490), center-cropped to the 2:3 portrait slot — still 100% real/correct-game official Steam art, just reframed rather than a purpose-built vertical capsule. No logo was available for Dragonwilds from Steam, so per instructions I skipped it rather than fabricate one.

I also updated `/opt/nxeon-staging/lib/games.ts` (`GAME_ART_SLUG`) to add the `poster` key for all 5 games — previously only `hero` was scaffolded, so posters would have silently fallen back to a wordmark placeholder even with the files present.
